analysis_options.funcdata: BfdArchitecture shells over the fixture-binary .text compiled from the probes in this fixture (g++ -O0 -fno-pie -no-pie); readLoaderSymbols(::) populates the symbol database queryCall reads; each shell follows flow from the probe symbol over the full default code space

observation.producer: official Ghidra 12.0.4 decompiler library (libdecomp.a at locked commit) driven by this fixture's BfdArchitecture shells
observation.format: Two case records in fixed probe order, pipe-free key=value lines: case/calls/spec/warn/blocks/block/op, final newline; 61 lines total
covered: tail jump into another function body: flow follows the branch, the callee body becomes blocks/ops of the caller (visited pollution is faithful Ghidra behavior, observable via op addr deltas and block ranges)

direct call whose entry is a visited instruction start AND a real loader symbol: queryCall resolves the callee, checkContainedCall's fd != 0 guard (flow.cc:1367-1368) skips it - the spec survives with the setFuncdata display name and the op keeps CPUI_CALL, zero warnings
recursive call back into the caller's own entry (trivially visited): same fd-resolved skip

control: direct call to a visited non-symbol interior start: no queryFunction hit, checkContainedCall converts CALL->BRANCH, emits the warningheader, restores the code-ref input, and erases the spec (calls=0)
spec creation order follows the LIFO addrlist: the callee-body recursion spec precedes the caller's direct-call spec
observation.discrimination: Against the pre-fix Rugra tree (query_call a documented no-op), the symbol case misfires: calls=1, warn text=pic:15, restructured blocks - the fixture fails. Against the fixed tree the output is byte-identical to the oracle.

decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: qlst is Funcdata-owned and passed by reference into FlowInfo (Rugra: fd.callspecs); visited is read-only in checkContainedCall; queryCall mutates the spec in place (setFuncdata entry+name, Rugra: set_funcdata + FlowInfo.resolved_funcdata set); data.warningHeader writes shared commentdb state; opSetOpcode/opMarkStartBasic/opSetInput/newCodeRef mutate shared PcodeOps - all observed through spec lists (op/entry deltas, display name), warning comments, op opcode/flag/input projections and the block graph.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: checkContainedCall iterates qlst in creation order (spec=0 is the callee-body recursion spec because the LIFO addrlist pops the tail-jump target before the je target); queryCall runs inside setupCallSpecs before checkForFlowModification; visited.upper_bound(addr) then one decrement equals BTreeMap range(..=addr).next_back().
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: No counters in the covered APIs; the resolved-callee marker (Ghidra fd pointer, Rugra resolved_funcdata set entry) is written once per spec by queryCall and never reset; entries for specs later erased by the offcut conversion are inert.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: visited is an address-ordered map keyed by instruction start; the containment test compares start + stat.size <= addr (byte range) and start == addr (exact instruction start); spec order is creation order, not address order.

status_note: Both behavioral projections (2 cases, 61 stdout lines) match the locked Ghidra 12.0.4 oracle byte-for-byte. The observation deliberately maps Ghidra's IPTR_FSPEC annotation and Rugra's Iop annotation to one callspec token (TYPEOP-FSPEC-SPACE-0001 residual, same precedent as flow_containedcall_1204); neither numeric payload is identity. Rugra's queryFunction equivalent is the driver-seeded Funcdata::symbol_table (CALLSPEC-DRIVER-0001 boundary); copyFlowEffects' inline/no-return flag copy has no data source at flow time yet (FLOW-NORETURN-DATA-0001).

out_of_scope_observations.note: Ghidra's oracle environment marks exit-class functions no-return via the name-driven 'Non-Returning Functions - Known' analyzer (locked program_flow_metadata_1204 fixture), and queryCall's copyFlowEffects then makes checkForFlowModification halt flow after those calls. Rugra's flow.rs now delegates is_inline/is_no_return to the real FuncProto flag bits, but no front-end feeds them at flow time, so a function ending in 'call exit' still falls through into the next function body (curl glob_word traces 344 vs golden 323 bytes). Fix requires driver-side seeding of known no-return names (out of this lease's write-set).
